Question: Thomson discusses a different version of the violinist case wherein the violinist only needs to use your kidneys for one hour to survive. Her own view about this case is that

Options: 
A. because the violinist's life is in danger, you have an absolute moral obligation to let them use your kidneys, regardless of the duration.
B. you have no obligation to let the violinist use your kidneys, but if you choose to do so, the violinist has the right to use them for that hour.
C. you have the right to disconnect the violinist at any point, regardless of the consequences for the violinist.
D. because you ought to let the violinist use your kidneys for that hour, we should conclude that he or she has a right to use your kidneys for that hour.
E. even though you ought to let the violinist use your kidneys for that hour, we should not conclude that he or she has a right to use your kidneys for that hour.
F. you have no obligation to let the violinist use your kidneys for that hour.
G. you have an obligation to let the violinist use your kidneys for that hour, but the violinist does not have a right to use your kidneys.
H. the violinist has an obligation to disconnect him- or herself before that hour is over.
I. you have an obligation to let the violinist use your kidneys for that hour, and the violinist also has a right to use your kidneys.

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.
